llm_summary: The run built a reasonably capable Act 1 deck and reached the Slime Boss with several upgraded defensive tools, but it spent too much HP on a chained event and later made a costly low-HP combat trade. The decisive combat error was using self-damaging Hemokinesis while at 12 HP and with defensive alternatives available, leaving only 10 HP before the encounter continued.

llm_lessons.title: Avoid self-damage when already near lethal range
llm_lessons.situation: When HP is very low and a turn offers both a self-damaging attack and a defensive card, especially when enemies are not clearly attacking.
llm_lessons.lesson: Treat Hemokinesis as a damage-race tool, not an automatic play: at critical HP, preserve survival unless its damage immediately removes a dangerous enemy. Prefer the available Defend or another non-self-damaging line when the target will survive anyway.
evidence_points: On turn 7 of the boss fight, HP was 12, both enemies had DEBUFF intents, and Hemokinesis and Defend were both legal with 2 energy.
Hemokinesis was played on the Acid Slime, reducing it from 40 to 25 HP while the player's HP fell from 12 to 10.
The following turn began at 10 HP with two additional Acid Slimes present, so the self-damage did not end the immediate threat.
llm_lessons.reasoning: The action exchanged 2 HP for partial progress against an enemy that remained alive, at a point where survival margin was already extremely small. This was a concrete, legal alternative where preserving HP was more valuable than modest extra damage.

llm_lessons.title: Stop escalating HP-loss event gambles
llm_lessons.situation: When an event offers repeated increasing HP costs for uncertain rewards and the first choice has already incurred a cost.
llm_lessons.lesson: After taking one risky branch, reassess rather than automatically continuing into higher-cost options; leave when the next gamble meaningfully reduces the HP buffer needed for upcoming elites or the boss.
evidence_points: The event choices successively cost 3 HP, then 4 HP, then 5 HP, reducing HP from 80 to 66.
Each deeper choice had only a stated 25%, 35%, or 45% chance to find a relic, so the trajectory records increasing costs but no guaranteed reward.
The run later reached the Slime Boss at 72 HP and died during the fight, making the earlier loss of HP a relevant reduction in its recovery and combat margin.
llm_lessons.reasoning: The event converted a full-health buffer into a 14-HP loss through repeated uncertain choices. Even though later resting recovered some HP, stopping earlier would have preserved more flexibility for the remainder of Act 1.
